topic: The Mary Celeste: a ship found in 1872 with nobody on board
pillar: Past: true mystery (the 'ghost' angle Rakesh wanted)
taste: No bodies, no ghosts drawn as real spirits; the people simply fade from a portrait. Bright day sea, not a dark night scene.

claims.claim: In December 1872 the crew of the Dei Gratia found the Mary Celeste drifting in the Atlantic (about 400 miles east of the Azores) with nobody on board.
About six months' supply of food and water was still on board.
Her cargo of 1,701 barrels of industrial alcohol was largely intact (only a few barrels empty).
Captain Benjamin Briggs, his wife, their two-year-old daughter and a crew of seven were never seen again.
The mystery has never been solved; theories (alcohol fumes, storm, mutiny) remain unproven.

rejected: Half-eaten breakfast / warm tea on the table - a myth popularised by Conan Doyle's 1884 story, not in the real reports.
Exact discovery date (sources split between 4 and 5 December) - script just says 1872.
